cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing, by hand, through form.
cells.place: In the seed state of all becoming — before any of it has chosen a shape.
cells.ask: Offer the tending to the next thing you're called to make or hold — let it be witnessed and received, so it is released by completion rather than kept by your grip.
cells.core: You're tending what's growing, and you're doing it by hand. Not forcing it and not hovering — steady care, given in form, given on time. Two things that both need you are being held at once, not by choosing one over the other, but by tending them in their own seasons. The care isn't exhausting you, because it isn't clutching. This balance is free to feed what comes next.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what's growing by hand, and the tending doesn't exhaust you.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.verb: Growing it before it's ready, on a schedule you set.
cells.place: In the seed state of all becoming — where nothing has chosen a shape yet, and you're already trying to shape it.
cells.ask: Let one thing you've been forcing ahead of its own timing rest and be completed on its own clock — so the vision comes from what you've actually lived through, not from what you're braced against.
cells.core: You're getting there ahead of the thing itself. Every start gets a plan, every plan gets a deadline, every deadline gets a version of you pushing — and the pushing is aimed at a future that hasn't arrived and won't take your shape. You're stewarding an outcome, not a growing thing. The care that doesn't exhaust is the kind that holds space without clutching; that's the side of this you're not on right now.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing growth on a schedule the thing itself didn't agree to.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: Setting down the tending that was yours to give.
cells.place: In the seed state of all becoming — where possibility sits untouched because you stopped reaching for it.
cells.ask: Return to the hope that fed it once — one small loyal tending, done whether or not it shines yet — so the radiance comes from what's actually been cultivated to completion.
cells.core: You stopped tending. Somewhere back there the care stopped landing, or stopped being seen, and you set it down — and the space where it used to live is still empty. The things that needed you didn't go away. You did. What's missing isn't the ability to grow something; it's the willingness to keep hoping while it's still unformed.
cells.sheetLine: You have what it takes to tend this, and you've stopped tending it.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: Shaping what's emerging — while calling it something that happened on its own.
cells.place: In the seed state of all becoming — where every possibility is still undecided, and your hand is on all of them.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've been quietly steering — say out loud that this is mine — so the intent is visible and honored, and what's finished can be let go as fulfillment rather than defeat.
cells.core: You're already tending something. You're the reason it's still alive, the reason it has a shape at all — and you talk about it as if it grew itself. The stewardship is running; the claim on it isn't. Recognizing it isn't taking credit. It's naming what your hands are already doing, so it can be released when it's done.
cells.sheetLine: You're already tending this. You just haven't said so.
